content.overview: Article 147 provides that in Chapter IV of Part V (Union Judiciary), references to any substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution shall be construed as including references to any substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Government of India Act, 1935 (including any enactment amending or supplementing that Act), or of any Order in Council or order made thereunder, or of the Indian Independence Act, 1947, or of any order made thereunder.
content.glance: In Union Judiciary chapter, ‘substantial question of law as to interpretation of the Constitution’ includes questions on GoI Act 1935 and Indian Independence Act 1947 (and related orders).
content.study:
Article 147 is an interpretation clause expanding the meaning of ‘substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution’ within the Union Judiciary chapter to cover legacy constitutional instruments (Government of India Act, 1935 and Indian Independence Act, 1947, and related orders).

Examination: expands constitutional-interpretation concept for legacy statutes; relevant to Arts 132, 145 etc.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: References to substantial questions of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution in this Chapter include substantial questions as to the interpretation of the Government of India Act, 1935 (and amending/supplementing enactments and Orders in Council/orders) and the Indian Independence Act, 1947 (and orders thereunder).

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 147 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 147 provides that in the Union Judiciary chapter, references to any substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution shall be construed as including references to any substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Government of India Act, 1935 (including amending or supplementing enactments and related Orders in Council or orders) or of the Indian Independence Act, 1947, or of any order made thereunder.

examTips: Expands ‘constitutional interpretation’ to GoI Act 1935 and Independence Act 1947.

keyTakeaways: Art 147: interpretation clause for legacy constitutional instruments in Union Judiciary chapter.
